page: Microsoft Azure D32s_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine hypervised on Microsoft Hyper-V, engineered for balanced enterprise workloads requiring steady CPU and memory capabilities. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. It delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores via hyperthreading, complemented by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI, alongside hardware-accelerated AES and SHA cryptographic support.

The virtual machine features 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no bundled local ephemeral storage, relying entirely on remote persistent storage solutions with Premium Storage support. Hardware accelerators are absent, with a zero GPU allocation. Benchmark profiles reveal solid memory subsystem behavior, placing the PassMark memory score in the upper quartile, backed by 144.07 GB/sec large-block read bandwidth and 67.37 GB/sec write bandwidth.

Compute benchmarks present steady mid-tier execution, scoring 1653 in Geekbench single-core and 14102 in multi-core routines. While lightweight language model inference on a 135M parameter model achieves strong text generation throughput at 275.82 tokens per second, large-scale models such as 70B yield diminished processing speeds of 6.58 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated tensor acceleration. Tradeoffs include total dependence on network-attached storage for disk operations and the absence of integrated local cache drives.

Azure D32s_v5 provides reliable density for general-purpose multi-threaded applications, enterprise backend services, Redis caching instances, build pipelines, relational database engines, and e-commerce web serving infrastructure requiring dependable compute-to-memory equilibrium.
description: Microsoft Azure D32s_v5 is a general-purpose instance providing 32 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. Sized with a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio across 16 physical cores, it incorporates a 260 MB L3 cache alongside AVX-512 vector support. The system contains no bundled local disks or GPUs, routing all storage operations through external premium managed storage. Benchmark evaluations show competitive memory performance in the upper quartile, alongside steady mid-tier results in multi-core compute tests and static web throughput of 33.3 GB/sec. Large model processing shows clear boundaries without discrete acceleration, confirming its primary focus as a balanced workhorse. This instance is best matched for enterprise application servers, mid-sized relational database environments, container fleets, and general web infrastructure.
